Its input direction isolates the native reconsideration/anti-Wait feature from matched unedited activations, removing the control mean and 16 dominant non-thinking directions. final_message:
Created /workspace/work/math_completion_adapter.npz: a rank-1 LoRA update to model.layers.22.mlp.down_proj only.

Diagnosis: all 20 initial competition-math probes exhausted 8,192 tokens without a boxed answer, commonly becoming trapped in repeated “Wait…” reconsideration. Independent problems confirmed the pattern. Closing an original thought at a useful prime-factorization checkpoint allowed all four unedited continuations to finish with the correct boxed answer.

The adapter uses a matched-context activation contrast dominated by the model’s existing layer-22 “Wait” suppressor. Common non-thinking activation directions are projected out. When this native braking signal is strong, the update supports ending the thought and producing the answer. Its output direction is locally orthogonal to 147 common text, arithmetic, message-ending, and code-delimiter readouts to limit collateral effects.

The update norm is 0.575, or 3.28% of the original weight’s Frobenius norm. Keys, shapes, rank, finite values, serialization, and both Frobenius and spectral norm limits were validated. No gradients, optimizers, training, or edited-model evaluation were used. Held-out accuracy improvement and preservation of other abilities remain unmeasured, as required by the one-shot rules. Construction details and limitations are recorded in README_adapter.md and adapter_metadata.json.
